title: fix(update): avoid bookkeeping-only repair refusals
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Released 2026.9.4 updaters can reject a successfully validated candidate with `repair-requires-config-change` when candidate Doctor changes only version, wizard, or migration bookkeeping in the rehearsal config.

Refs #169953. The reported `config.auth` hang remains unconfirmed and is outside this change.

## User Impact

Candidate validation preserves bookkeeping in the copied config, allowing older updaters to compare it without a false repair requirement. Real config migrations, webhook endpoint repairs, and plugin enablement remain intact. Normal writes after activation still persist current metadata. No new configuration, CLI options, schema, or dependencies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The candidate recognizes the complete rehearsal environment already supplied by released drivers. Config stamping defers metadata-only additions, Doctor leaves wizard history unchanged, and the existing state owner records webhook completion when no endpoint changed. Semantic migration changes and removal of deferred-migration markers still persist.

The reproduced `plugins` difference was actual activation: `plugins.allow` gained `openai` and `codex`, with their entries enabled. It was not install-record bookkeeping, so this behavior is preserved. The published-driver proof pre-enables those plugins to isolate bookkeeping.

The changed-path collector is moved unchanged to its existing owner to keep the writer within its line cap. The one-line `TransactionRecipes` visibility cleanup matches main commit `4cdac89cf0b656ef90cb22bb4fd3dfa9e7205bf9` and resolves the inherited dead-export gate.

## Evidence

- Published 2026.9.4 validator, unchanged body exposed by an export-only observation hook, against the built 2026.10.2 candidate in isolated synthetic state: `status=ok`, `phase=readiness`, `changedKeys=[]`, total **113.799 s**, `config.auth` **1.573 s**. All six validation steps exited 0; Gateway canary completed in **17.330 s**. Node 24.21.0. The released driver projects Gateway auth for the canary while channel store references remain. This proves candidate validation/rehearsal, not a full installation/service handoff.
- The final Doctor regression fails on the original main source at both intended comparisons: `meta` adds the candidate version/utility marker and `wizard` changes its version/time. Source was restored byte-for-byte afterward. Baseline wall time **44.50 s**, test time **7.614 s**.
- Final focused proof: Doctor group **6/6 passed** (101.65 s wall; new regression 6.737 s test time); webhook group **23/23 passed** (13.15 s wall). Gateway importer: **11 passed, 2 failed** in **435.40 s**. The unchanged workspace-plugin POST /tools/invoke test hit its 90 s timeout and 180 s cleanup timeout (270.004 s total); the following wizard test failed with `Session history database read was revoked` (34.098 s). A sample found the worker idle in the event loop with plugin-capture state still open. This remains an unresolved startup/cleanup gap; no speculative Gateway fix or timeout change is included. The overall final batch exited 1; these results are not claimed green.
- Final exact-source runtime rebuild: all four compiler invocations and all post-build phases passed in **5m 42.2s**, before test execution.
- `CI=1 node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 4f1b5766b6b9d166d15c6adc214f6f7983133aa6 --timed`: all gates passed, including core and 28 test-type graphs, formatting, lint, dead exports, and runtime import cycles.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-madge-import-cycles.ts`: **0 cycles**.
- The required importer run covered 36 selected files: 305 tests passed, 7 failed, and 5 were platform-skipped before the remaining plugin/Gateway groups could run. The failures were in billing-route, Canvas migration, legacy composition, model-metadata persistence, and setup recovery. Billing fixture diagnostics show the timed-out body still running when its successor starts, then losing HOME/lease ownership (late settlement at 144.035 s). The Canvas/setup comparison passed all 5 tests on original main in 95.39 s; the same five tests also passed on the patched source alongside the new regression (six tests, 101.65 s file-group wall time; the new regression itself took 6.737 s). These are recorded unresolved batch/fixture failures, not claimed fixes. Existing slow tests included billing cases at 103.967–121.652 s and the model-metadata timeout at 128.318 s; the first runtime build took 17m 16s, separately from test execution.
- Fresh isolated Codex autoreview: no actionable P0–P2 findings.

- CI follow-up: [run 38301453125, failing shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38301453125/job/114985525771) reported a 20 s `config.patch` request timeout in “reloads owners independently and reports a changed unresolved owner as cold.” That exact case passed locally on head `3f071473` in **59.516 s** and on pre-change parent `4f1b5766` in **51.550 s**, including Gateway setup. The full-file head run had **65 passed / 2 failed**, **622.17 s** Vitest wall time (**648.92 s** including preparation); the parent-production run had **65 passed / 2 failed**, **554.67 s** Vitest wall time (**719.61 s** including preparation). Both runs failed the later “agents.delete preserves newer writes across a large shrink” cases: `authority revoked: false` timed out in `config.patch`, then hit the 180 s `server.close` timeout (**197.295 s** head / **207.000 s** parent); `authority revoked: true` then failed startup because plugin metadata was still shutting down (**113.498 s** / **108.908 s**). These local failures are inherited; the reported CI case remains unreproduced.
- Ordinary writes were observed on disk with both migration stamps and `meta.lastTouchedVersion=2026.10.2` before the local request timed out. Both head and parent Gateway logs then showed config reload evaluation waiting until shutdown marked application stopped. The PR's metadata selector is synchronous, returns the normal stamped result outside the complete rehearsal contract, and adds no deferred promise or activation wait. No speculative production change, timeout increase, or retry was added. CI tested merge `ba381b1e` (PR into `17c9b482`); these local comparisons used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` with the unchanged test file and all seven PR production files substituted from parent `4f1b5766` (then restored byte-for-byte), isolating the PR against its parent. They do not reproduce that exact Linux merge environment.

Diff size: production +61/−13 lines, tests +118 lines, documentation +6 lines. The CI gate is currently red on the timeout described above; the local comparison does not claim a green CI rerun. All proof ran locally; no remote lease or operator Gateway/state was used.
